newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi American Bank to let foreigners in new fund.
newsitem.headline: Saudi American Bank to let foreigners in new fund.

text.p: Saudi American Bank (SAMBA) said on Sunday it had received Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency (SAMA) approval to set up what it said would be the first investment fund to allow foreign participation in Saudi equities.
The closed-ended fund will be called the Saudi Arabian Investment Fund Ltd (SAIF Ltd), the bank said in a statement.
SAMA is the kingdom's central bank.
"SAIF Ltd will invest exclusively in the units of SAIF KSA, which will in turn invest primarily in the shares of Saudi companies," the statement said.

"SAIF Ltd will be listed on the London Stock Exchange and will be open to Saudi and non-Saudi participation. This is the first time that non-Saudis have been provided the opportunity to participate in the Saudi stock market," it added.

A SAMBA official, speaking by telephone from Riyadh, would not give the planned size of the fund, when subscription would open, nor when the fund was likely to be listed in London. He would not say when SAMA approval was given.
The Gulf's biggest bourse is so far restricted to Saudis and other Gulf Arabs. There are some 70 firms listed on the market, capitalised at around $42 billion.

Only Saudi nationals can hold shares in all local firms. Nationals of the other five Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states can own Saudi equities, excluding banks -- which account for about a third of market capitalisation -- and certain other stocks.
The GCC is made up of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates.
The Riyadh-based SAMBA is 30 percent owned by Citicorp unit Citibank.
